newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Barak demands Netanyahu "control tongue".
newsitem.headline: Israel's Barak demands Netanyahu "control tongue".

text.p: Ehud Barak, vying to lead Israel's main opposition Labour party, accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday of endangering Israel and its relations with Washington and Arab states.
Netanyahu's office struck back swiftly, saying Barak's party had taken Israel's security to an all-time low before it was ousted from power by Netanyahu in May elections.

"There is room for the ordinary citizen to be worried," Barak said. "Netanyahu in a few months under the headline of a different approach has succeeded in sum to deteriorate our relations with the Arab world and to deteriorate trust.
"I...call on the prime minister to control his tongue and act responsibly," Barak, foreign minister in the previous government and a former army chief of staff, told Israel Radio.
Barak made the comments in part because of Syrian troop movements in Lebanon and Syria that Israel is closely watching.

"It is not a situation without risks...It demands responsible behaviour from the upper echelons, first of all from the prime minister," said Barak, 54, vying to take over Labour from Shimon Peres, 73, in party elections due next summer.

Syrian troops left a number of positions in the central Lebanese mountains last month. But Lebanese sources said this was a defensive redeployment after apparent Israeli threats to attack Syrian forces in Lebanon.
Barak blasted Netanyahu's vow on Sunday that he would risk ties with Washington if they conflicted with his goals.
"Israel's security is more important than anything, but relations with the United States is one of the central pillars of Israel's security," Barak said.
"Therefore any position that says those things contradict one another or could potentially contradict one another is damaging and a prophecy that could be self-fulfilling."
Barak also took aim at Netanyahu's attitude towards Egypt, the first Arab state to sign a peace treaty with Israel in 1979.
"I do not see any reason to speak to the Egyptians in a vulgar manner. Prime ministers do not talk about cutting off your nose to spite your face," he said.

Netanyahu on Sunday chided Egypt for tying a planned regional economic summit to moves in the peace process by the Jewish state. Netanyahu said if Egypt cancelled the summit it would be "like a man who cuts off his nose to spite his face".
Netanyahu's spokesman said in a reaction to Barak:
"The Labour government and Barak as a part of it brought an unprecedented deterioration in the state of Israel's security. The people of Israel understood this and changed the government.
"The citizens of Israel chose another policy over the policy of concessions that he and his friends led. The present government intends to bring peace in a more secure way."

Arab League foreign ministers in Cairo on Sunday, angered that Netanyahu has yet to redeploy troops under peace deals with the PLO and is standing by opposition to trading occupied Arab land for peace, repeated they might reconsider concessions made to Israel in peace negotiations with the previous government.
